note:
Docstring strip. 4867 -> 4750 (-117), measured on a CLEAN WORKTREE at HEAD 33384e98f13 -- the shared checkout measured 4700 at the same moment, because it carried a second round of uncommitted removals, and flooring on that would have recorded a number no commit reproduces. That is the trap ruff.toml header records as having mis-set the ruff floor twice; it applies to every floor, not just ruff.

Decomposed, because the -117 is two unrelated movements:
  - +27 first: the floor was seeded at 4867 by b2817f28783 and never re-floored, while HEAD drifted to 4894 across the ~150 commits since. Mainline was red on this gate for that whole stretch. That regression is not attributed to any one commit here -- it accumulated -- and it is absorbed by this move rather than hunted down.
  - -144 second: a7f5fff805f stripped docstrings from odoo/odoo. 4894 -> 4750 with NO logic change of any kind.

That second number is worth reading twice. py_function_length measures `end_lineno - lineno + 1`, every line the function spans, and the module docstring defends that on purpose: "Skipping blanks or comments would let a long function hide behind its own documentation, and the budget is about how much a reader must hold at once." The consequence, now that pydocstyle is retired (b6ba608ee27) and docstrings are being removed rather than added, is that this gate is the only one still pricing them -- and it prices them as complexity. Deleting prose reads here as 144 lines of improvement; adding a docstring to an over-budget function reads as a regression. Nobody has decided that is wrong, so nothing is changed here beyond the floor, but the next person to move this number should know the metric moves on documentation as readily as on code.
